body:
PR #1990 for TASK-1296, and the lane found a defect the spec did not describe

Open on branch task-1296, +368, both new functions in lib.rs. Same handover: I wrote the prompt, no verdict from me. Relayed context below is relayed — nothing in it rests on the operator's word.

WHAT IT DOES. Hooks into `auto_bump_done_to_completed`, the function `aida pull` and `aida db sync --pull` already call, exactly where you said the information already lives. For any Review-PR spec still Approved or InProgress that the git-log scan cannot resolve, it asks the forge directly via Forge::change_metadata: MERGED closes it Completed, CLOSED-unmerged closes it Rejected with an audit comment naming the PR and reason, OPEN is untouched. No change to `queue gc` — once the status flips terminal, gc's existing target-spec rule prunes the entry on its next pass, which is the acceptance criterion rather than a second mechanism.

THE PART WORTH YOUR ATTENTION, because the spec did not ask for it and it is the reason the feature would otherwise have shipped broken. I verified this in the diff:

  - if candidates.is_empty() && pr_to_sha.is_empty() { return ... }

A closed-unmerged PR never produces a `(#N)` merge commit, so it can never appear in pr_to_sha, and it produces no Done candidate either. Both collections stay empty precisely in the case the spec exists to handle, so the pre-existing early-return would have skipped detection entirely. The fix moves the store load and the forge lookup ahead of that early-out.

That is a nice instance of the class PRIN-4 names, from the other direction: the guard was correct for every case anyone had considered, and silently wrong for the one case being added. Worth noting that it was found by implementing, not by review — the reviewer would have seen a function that looked right.

Test uses a fake gh binary via AIDA_TEST_GH_BINARY to model all six real fixture specs (STORY-1234/1238/1240/1343/1344/1345 against PRs 1952/1949/1957/1964/1956/1965) plus a still-open control, without touching any real spec. Reported and not re-run by me: 5086 tests pass, fmt clean.

The pre-commit provenance gate caught trace markers on `///` doc comments again and the lane fixed them. That is now four lanes out of seven. It is doing real work rather than being a formality, and none of those would have been caught by review.

FANOUT RESULT, TWO LANES. Both delivered, neither stalled: #1988 for BUG-1279 and #1990 for TASK-1296. The difference from this afternoon's three-of-five is the prompt — I stated the headless-waiting rule as a hard constraint and named the precedent ("two earlier lanes stalled exactly this way, the second despite being told not to") rather than as advice near the top. That is still an instruction rather than a mechanical guard, so I would not call it solved; it is a better instruction, which is the weaker of the two fixes and the only one available inside a prompt.

Both PRs are yours. #1988 in particular deserves a reader who is not me, since it corrected my own briefing on whether .aida/discipline/ is tracked, and I would rather someone checked that correction than took it from the lane that made it.
